title: SEC drops crypto-exchange cases; donors
summary: The SEC did drop or close its cases against Coinbase (Feb 27, 2025), Kraken (Mar 27, 2025), Binance (May 29, 2025) and Gemini (investigation closed Feb 2025; Earn suit dismissed Jan 2026), plus many other crypto matters. Coinbase, Kraken, Crypto.com and Ripple each gave $1M or more to the inauguration, the Winklevoss twins gave about $1M each to the 2024 campaign (the excess was refunded), Coinbase sponsored the Army parade, and Coinbase, Ripple, Tether and the Winklevosses gave to the ballroom. The video overstates it in three ways: some dismissals came months later; formal lawsuit dismissals number about 7-8 (over a dozen only if closed probes are counted); and no Binance donation was found. The quid-pro-quo framing rests on timing, not on proof, and the SEC denies any political favoritism.

sub_claims.statement: Coinbase, Kraken, Binance and Gemini all faced SEC enforcement.
sub_claims.finding: The SEC sued Coinbase (Jun 2023), Kraken/Payward (Nov 2023), Binance and Zhao (Jun 2023), and Gemini over Gemini Earn (Jan 2023). Gemini also faced a separate investigation, with a Wells notice in 2024.

sub_claims.statement: The cases were dropped one by one, very shortly after Trump took office.
sub_claims.finding: Coinbase was dismissed with prejudice on Feb 27, 2025. Gemini's investigation was closed on Feb 26, 2025. Kraken was dismissed with prejudice on Mar 27, 2025, together with Consensys and Cumberland. Binance was stayed in Feb 2025 and dismissed with prejudice on May 29, 2025. Ripple's appeals were dropped on Aug 7, 2025, with the $125M judgment intact. The Gemini Earn suit was dismissed by stipulation on Jan 23, 2026. The first wave came within weeks; other cases took months, up to a year.

sub_claims.statement: Over a dozen lawsuits against cryptocurrency exchanges were dropped.
sub_claims.finding: The SEC's own FY2025 accounting lists 7 crypto enforcement actions dismissed between Feb and May 2025: Coinbase, Binance, Cumberland, Consensys, Kraken, Dragonchain and Balina. Gemini Earn was added in Jan 2026. Decrypt counts at least 17 firms once closed probes are included (Robinhood, Uniswap, OpenSea, Crypto.com, Yuga, Gemini). The NYT, as reported secondhand, found about 60% of inherited crypto cases paused, dropped or dismissed. Over a dozen holds for crypto companies and probes combined, but not for lawsuits against exchanges specifically.

sub_claims.statement: Multiple of these exchanges gave $1M or more to Trump's campaign or inauguration fund.
sub_claims.finding: Coinbase, Kraken and Crypto.com each gave $1M to the inaugural committee, and Ripple gave about $4.9-5M in XRP. Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss (Gemini) each gave about $1M in BTC to the Trump campaign in Jun 2024; about $155K each over the $844,600 limit was refunded. No Binance contribution to the campaign or inauguration was found.

Coinbase was a named sponsor of the June 14, 2025 Army 250th parade and festival, via a donation to the nonpartisan America250. No other exchange was found among the sponsors. Total sponsorship was reported at about $885K.

sub_claims.statement: They sponsored the White House ballroom.
sub_claims.finding: The White House's Oct 2025 list of 37 ballroom donors includes Coinbase, Ripple, Tether America, and Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss. Kraken and Binance were not found on it.

sub_claims.statement: The dismissals coincide with what looks like quid-pro-quo deals.
sub_claims.finding: The donations and the timing are documented. No evidence was found that any dismissal was exchanged for a donation. The SEC cites policy and discretion, and firms with no known Trump donations (Uniswap, OpenSea) also had their probes dropped.

corrections: Transcript says the cases were dropped 'very shortly after Trump took office'. Coinbase, Kraken and the Gemini investigation fell within about 10 weeks, but Binance's dismissal came in May 2025, Ripple's in August 2025 (with the $125M penalty upheld), and the Gemini Earn suit's in January 2026.

Transcript says 'over a dozen lawsuits against cryptocurrency exchanges'. The SEC formally dismissed about 7-8 crypto lawsuits. Counts above a dozen (Decrypt: at least 17) include closed investigations and non-exchange firms.
Gemini's $1M gifts were personal 2024 campaign contributions from the Winklevoss twins, partly refunded as over the limit, not donations from the company to the inauguration.
No Binance donation to Trump's campaign or inauguration was found; Binance's Trump links run through the MGX/USD1 deal and the CZ pardon.
Of the exchanges, only Coinbase is documented as a sponsor of the military parade.
denials_and_context: The SEC says political favoritism played no role and that its decisions rest on legal and policy considerations; its dismissals cite 'the exercise of its discretion and as a policy matter.'

The SEC later acknowledged 'flaws' in its earlier crypto enforcement. The industry calls the Gensler-era cases 'regulation by enforcement', and courts had split on the legal theories (e.g., the Ripple programmatic-sales ruling).
The Gemini Earn dismissal followed full return of investor assets through the Genesis bankruptcy, and Gemini had already paid NYAG settlements.
The parade sponsorship went through the nonpartisan America250, and the ballroom donor list includes many non-crypto firms.
Public Citizen and Democrats argue that crypto's political spending 'paid off'; that is advocacy, not proof of a quid pro quo.
